canonical_question: Why is the mass loss increase from 450 °C to 650 °C for DS2205 (~24 to ~69 mg/cm²) significantly larger than for the HEA (~19 to ~38 mg/cm²)?

question_variants.question: Why is the mass loss increase from 450 °C to 650 °C for DS2205 (~24 to ~69 mg/cm²) significantly larger than for the HEA (~19 to ~38 mg/cm²)?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The document provides the mass loss values showing the difference (~69 vs ~38 mg/cm²) but does not explicitly explain the mechanistic reason for the larger increase in DS2205 compared to the HEA.

answers.answer: The document reports the mass loss values: DS2205 increased to ~69 mg/cm² while AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 increased to ~38 mg/cm², but does not provide the underlying cause for the magnitude difference in this specific context.
answers.mechanism: selective dissolution of α-Ferrite phase attributed to micro-galvanic coupling
answers.boundary_limitation: Results specific to molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 salt
evidence_spans: Here, the molten salt corrosion behavior of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was evaluated in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt at 450 °C and 650 °C in comparison to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205).
The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205.
Similarly, EHEA showed a lower corrosion rate of ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205.

source_evidence_spans: At 650 °C, mass loss drastically increased for DS2205 to ~69 mg/cm 2 after 24 h compared to ~38 mg/cm 2 for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1
